data.label: Receive CSV File
data.description: Trigger when a new incoming CSV file is received for validation.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic event trigger based on file arrival. No ML, NLP, or LLM capability is required. It is pure workflow orchestration and therefore L0.
conditions: file extension is .csv or content-type indicates CSV
data.errorHandling: If the file is missing, unreadable, or not a CSV, reject early with a file-ingestion error and stop the workflow. Log the failure and emit a structured invalid-input result.

data.label: Load Validation Schema
data.description: Retrieve the expected column list, data types, required fields, and numeric range rules.
data.rationale: Loading validation rules from a predefined source is deterministic lookup behavior. L0 is sufficient because this step does not involve uncertainty, language understanding, or learned prediction.
data.errorHandling: If schema lookup fails, retry once after a brief backoff. If it still fails, produce a schema-load error and terminate with a failed validation report stub.

data.label: Parse CSV Content
data.description: Read and structure the incoming CSV file into rows and columns for validation.
data.rationale: CSV parsing is deterministic file processing with known delimiters and schema structure. This is classic rule-based data extraction and requires no AI.
conditions: CSV delimiter and encoding are supported
data.errorHandling: If parsing fails due to malformed CSV, capture the parser error, mark the file as invalid, and continue to report generation with parse errors included. Retry only for transient I/O failures, not malformed content.

data.label: Check Expected Columns
data.description: Compare CSV headers against the expected schema and identify missing or unexpected columns.
data.rationale: This is a direct schema comparison using exact matching and set operations. It is fully deterministic and fits L0 with no need for ML or language reasoning.
data.errorHandling: If headers are missing or duplicate, record column-level validation errors. Do not stop the workflow unless the file cannot be structurally interpreted. Missing required columns are treated as validation failures and propagated forward.

data.label: Validate Data Types
data.description: Verify that each column value matches the data type defined in the schema.
data.rationale: Data type validation is a deterministic rules/regex/parsing task. Since the schema defines the expected types, this can be handled entirely with L0 logic.
data.errorHandling: Record per-cell type mismatches and continue validating remaining rows. Use safe coercion only when explicitly permitted by schema; otherwise preserve raw values and flag errors. Retry is not applicable except for transient runtime failures.

data.label: Check Required Nulls
data.description: Flag null, empty, or missing values in fields marked as required.
data.rationale: Required-field null checking is simple deterministic validation. No uncertainty or model inference is needed, so L0 is the correct level.
data.errorHandling: Flag missing, blank, or whitespace-only values in required fields. If a row is structurally corrupted, mark the row-level issue and continue scanning the rest of the dataset.

data.label: Validate Numeric Ranges
data.description: Check numeric fields against acceptable minimum and maximum values from the schema.
data.rationale: Numeric range checks are pure rule-based comparisons against thresholds from the schema. This is fully deterministic L0 automation.
conditions: numeric fields are defined in schema
data.errorHandling: If a numeric field is non-numeric, it should already be captured by type validation; still record a range-check skip note if needed. For out-of-range values, log row, column, observed value, and allowed bounds. No retry required.

data.label: Aggregate Validation Errors
data.description: Collect all validation failures from column, type, null, and range checks into a single error set.
data.rationale: Aggregating validation results is deterministic data collection and concatenation. It does not require learning or language generation, so L0 is sufficient.
conditions: validation results from prior steps exist
data.errorHandling: If aggregation fails, fall back to a minimal error summary containing step-level failure markers and counts. Preserve all previously collected issues whenever possible.

data.label: Generate Validation Report
data.description: Create a validation report listing all discovered errors and the overall file status.
data.rationale: Although this step produces a report, the output is a template-driven compilation of known validation results rather than open-ended language generation. It remains deterministic formatting and therefore L0.
data.errorHandling: If report rendering fails, emit a structured JSON fallback report with validation status, error count, and failed step names. Prefer machine-readable output over formatted documents.

data.label: Publish Validation Result
data.description: Output the completed validation report for downstream review or processing.
data.rationale: Publishing the final report is a deterministic workflow end action. It simply passes the produced artifact downstream, requiring no AI or probabilistic reasoning.
data.errorHandling: If publishing fails, retry with exponential backoff for transient transport errors. If still unsuccessful, persist the report locally or to durable storage and mark the workflow as publish-failed.

data.condition: true; proceed even if column issues exist so all errors can be collected
data.label: continue with validation
run null checks in parallel with type outcomes
run range checks in parallel with null checks

data.label: retry with updated schema

message: This workflow validates incoming CSV files using deterministic L0 tooling. The pipeline loads schema rules, parses the CSV, checks headers, validates types, scans required-field nulls, checks numeric ranges, aggregates all issues, and generates a final validation report. Parallel execution is introduced after type validation so null checks and range checks can run concurrently. Error paths preserve partial results and fall back to structured reports when parsing, schema loading, or report rendering fails.
